items.summary: OS command injection in Dokploy's patch.readRepoDirectories tRPC procedure lets an authenticated organization member inject shell metacharacters into the user-controlled repoPath value and execute arbitrary commands as root in the Dokploy container — and via the mounted Docker socket, compromise the host. Fixed in Dokploy 0.29.13.

Pre-authentication path traversal plus unsafe file upload in the Check Point Management web service allows an unauthenticated attacker with network access to upload files to arbitrary paths and execute arbitrary scripts or load an arbitrary Java class. Confirmed exploited as a zero-day in targeted attacks as early as July 23, 2026; patches released September 22 and added to CISA KEV.

Unauthenticated remote code execution in JetBrains TeamCity on-premises servers (patch released July 28). CISA warned on September 24, 2026 that ransomware groups are actively exploiting it, and it is listed in the CISA Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog.

Heap-based buffer overflow in F5 BIG-IP Access Policy Manager lets an unauthenticated attacker with network access achieve remote code execution by sending crafted traffic to a virtual server with both an APM access policy and an OAuth profile configured. Added to CISA KEV on September 22, 2026 with active exploitation confirmed.

Unauthenticated remote code execution in Next.js 16.2.0–16.3.5 via improper escaping in SVG output generated by Satori in the Node.js next/og ImageResponse implementation. Vercel published an emergency fix (16.3.6) on September 22, 2026; Edge runtime unaffected.
